findings.description: The synthetic TextPart's `messageID` falls back only to `input.messageID`, which is optional in the opencode chat.message hook signature. When opencode invokes the hook without `messageID` (or when no prior part exists to copy from), the pushed part has `messageID: undefined`. OpenCode's TextPart Zod schema requires `messageID: string` (per @opencode-ai/sdk's TextPart), and as of opencode 1.2.27 the runtime validates part IDs/required fields before save, so the whole user message is rejected with a ZodError and the image description plus the prompt are lost. The hook already has `output.message: UserMessage` whose `id` is always defined and is the canonical source - the fallback chain should be `anchor?.messageID ?? output.message?.id ?? input.messageID`.

`handleToolExecuteBefore` checks `output.args.path` as a fallback after `filePath`, but opencode's built-in Read tool only ever passes `filePath` (see packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts: Parameters.filePath is the only string field). The `path` branch is unreachable against the real tool surface and just adds noise to the generated plugin file shipped to users.

testing_summary: No tests were executed during review (per the review-phase rule). I traced the new logic by reading the generated plugin source, the @opencode-ai/plugin and @opencode-ai/sdk type definitions (text Part schema, chat.message / tool.execute.before hook shapes), the prior opencode community reports of `prt` prefix and `synthetic` part validation, and the integration.test.ts coverage.
risk_rationale: The change adds a substantial new agent integration that spawns a real subprocess per image and mutates opencode's part array, with a reachable bug in the synthetic-part messageID fallback that can break the chat.message hook under opencode's runtime Zod validation; otherwise the design, fail-open semantics, version-marker handling, and test coverage are reasonable.
